title: Use Desmos Lists and List Tools
description: Create named lists, transform every value with list arithmetic, combine lists with join, and calculate mean, median, and total efficiently in Desmos.

questions.stem_html: A list contains [5, 8, 11]. Each value is multiplied by 2 and then increased by 4. What is the mean of the resulting values?
questions.explanation_html: Apply both operations to each entry, then take the mean. The resulting list is [14, 20, 26].
questions.variation: Transform an entire list and find its mean

questions.stem_html: Each value in a list was multiplied by 5 and then increased by 7. The resulting values are [17, 37, 57]. What was the mean of the original list?
questions.explanation_html: Undo the last change first: subtract 7 from every value, then divide the whole list by 5. The original list is [2, 6, 10]. Its mean is \(6\).
questions.variation: Reverse an entire list transformation and read a statistic

questions.stem_html: A list contains [12, 15, 17]. Add 4 to each value, then multiply each result by 3. What is the total of the transformed list?
questions.explanation_html: The transformed values are [48, 57, 63]. Their sum is 168.
questions.variation: Apply list arithmetic and total the results

questions.stem_html: Two lists give Monday and Tuesday counts for the same stations in the same order. The lists are [5, 7, 11] and [9, 2, 3]. What is the median of the stations’ two-day totals?
questions.explanation_html: Add matching positions to get [14, 9, 14]. Their middle value in sorted order is 14.
questions.variation: Combine matching list positions and calculate their median

questions.stem_html: An experiment recorded [4, 8, 12] in its first group and [1, 15] in its second group. What is the median across all individual observations?
questions.explanation_html: Join the two full lists and sort their values: [1, 4, 8, 12, 15]. The middle entry is 8.
questions.variation: Join whole groups before calculating a statistic
